sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Zaandam, the largest town of the municipality of Zaanstad, has tightened and simplified its parking rates in the past year. The council adopted the parking tax ordinance for 2026 on 27 November 2025; the version in force from 1 May 2026 charges 3.50 euros an hour in tariff zone I and 2.55 euros in zone II, with a 10.00 euro day ticket in designated car parks [0]. The ordinance has been through several versions: three zones at 3.70, 3.10 and 2.50 euros from December 2024, a version at 3.80, 3.15 and 2.55 euros that applied only from 4 to 15 December 2025, and the two-zone version from 16 December 2025 [1]. Zone I is paid Monday to Saturday from 9:00 to 23:00 and Sunday from 12:00 to 17:00, zone II until 19:00, under a decision in force from 1 March 2026, which exempts the Oostzijderveld area until signs and equipment have been installed [6][7]. A resident permit costs 118.80 euros a year, with at most two per address in nine areas of Zaandam, and no permits are issued for paid streets outside them [2][9]. From 1 November 2026 payment at parking equipment is electronic only [8]. A camera car checks paid areas seven days a week and five or more unpaid fines lead to a wheel clamp [12]. The centre is closed to through car and motorcycle traffic daily from 12:00 to 18:00, using retractable bollards, with all streets reachable by other routes [17]. Blue zones with two free hours and a disc apply on the Zuiddijk and in shopping areas elsewhere in the municipality [10].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The main project is a public underground car park under the Peperstraat in central Zaandam. A developer's explanatory note of February 2026 describes 334 spaces, 33 of them with charging, serving 567 new homes and centre visitors through double use, with the permit granted in July 2024 [18]. The municipality amended the permit on 16 April 2026 for six residential buildings with 355 homes and an underground car park in this phase, and appeals against both the zoning plan and the original permit were still pending at the Council of State [19]. On charging, the ordinance exempted electric vehicles from parking tax while they charge at a municipal bay in a paid area until 30 April 2026, and from 1 May 2026 parking fees apply on charging bays in paid-parking areas [3][4]. The college designated two charging-only spaces at the Oost-Dorsch car park on 10 June 2026 and withdrew that decision on 15 July 2026 without a published reason [5]. The older parking policy note, written in 2016, planned a parking route information system with occupancy data that could be offered as open data, and we did not verify its current state [16].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality says the Burcht and Behouden Haven car parks sell day tickets, that Q-Park runs the Rozenhof and Hermitage garages and that the Zaantheater runs its own garage [11]. Q-Park lists the Hermitage with 893 spaces and 65 charging points, the Rozenhof with 487, and a P+R at Provincialeweg with 119, all open round the clock; its tariffs did not load [13]. NS lists the P+R Provincialeweg at 3.45 euros an hour, 14.00 euros a day and 6.00 euros a day for rail travellers from 1 May 2026 [14]. The old policy note said the municipality had no influence on tariffs in the Q-Park garages [15].

Our data cover the P+R Provincialeweg, with 118 spaces, for about 53 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 27% on weekdays and 25% at weekends, and it reached full in a single reading on a Sunday morning. The garages and street parking are not in our data.
